NAV·IT vs Google MapsA sovereign navigator in build and the mainstream map, compared

NAV·IT is a self-hosted turn-by-turn navigator from VF Empire, built on open map data with VF's own routing, tiles and edge in EU jurisdiction; every route your phone traces stays inside VF infrastructure, never sent to Google, Apple or Mapbox. It ships inside FuelIT and MapIT and is in build. Google Maps is the mapping and navigation service operated by Google LLC, a United States company owned by Alphabet. This page compares the two on map data, where routing runs, what the provider can see, offline mode, business model, open-source status and jurisdiction.

NAV·IT · In build Open map data (OSM) Self-hosted · EU Google: United States

DEFINITIONS

What each one is.
In one paragraph.

One is a mature worldwide service used by billions of devices; the other is infrastructure VF built so that its own apps could keep a privacy promise. The comparison is fair only if that difference in maturity stays visible, so every NAV·IT row on this page carries its build status.

P·21 · VF EMPIRE

NAV·IT

NAV·IT exists because FuelIT could not credibly promise "no data sold" while handing every drive to a third-party map. VF built the whole navigator: an OpenStreetMap planet mirror on its own build box, Valhalla routing, Photon search and PMTiles on a Hetzner AX102 in Germany, a Cloudflare Worker gateway that strips your IP before the origin sees it, and clients that verify every routing response against an Ed25519 key compiled into the app.

Three modes carry one guarantee: full-offline produces zero network traffic during navigation, hybrid (the default) routes through the anonymising gateway, and online offers the same guarantee without a local cache. The engineering spec, threat model, privacy model and a seven-check verification checklist are published (the same STRIDE shape VF drafts for clients in the Threat Model + DPIA engagement), with a bug bounty from €500 to €25 000 for anyone who breaks a claim. NAV·IT is in build; R·01 ships inside FuelIT for nine countries.

Source: the NAV·IT product page, its published spec and privacy model, and the security posture.
GOOGLE LLC · UNITED STATES

Google Maps

Google Maps is the mapping and navigation service operated by Google LLC, a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc., headquartered in Mountain View, California. As Google describes in its documentation, it runs on Google's own proprietary map data combined with licensed sources and user contributions, computes routes on Google's servers when the device is online, and offers downloadable offline areas that include driving directions.

Google describes account-level controls, including Timeline (formerly Location History) and Web & App Activity, that govern what location and search activity is saved to a Google account, and has announced that Timeline data is stored on the user's device. The consumer app is free to use; Alphabet reports advertising as its largest source of revenue, and Google licenses the Maps Platform APIs to developers. The service has operated since 2005.

Source: Google's own public documentation, terms and announcements. VF makes no claim about Google's security beyond what Google states.
THE COMPARISON

Architecture,
row by row.

NAV·IT facts come from the product page and its published documents. Google Maps facts are limited to what Google documents publicly. Status chips mark what NAV·IT has not yet shipped.

QuestionNAV·ITGoogle Maps
Where does the map data come from? OpenStreetMap, mirrored on VF's own build box with weekly diffs. Every published pack ships with the SHA-256 of the exact planet file it was built from and the git SHA of the tools that built it. No proprietary data licence to renew. Google's proprietary map data, combined with licensed sources and user contributions, as Google describes in its documentation.
Where does routing run? Full-offline mode: on the device, with zero network traffic. Hybrid and online modes: on VF's origin server (Valhalla on a Hetzner AX102 in Nürnberg, Germany), reached through a Cloudflare Worker gateway that strips CF-Connecting-IP, X-Forwarded-For and User-Agent before the origin sees them. In build On Google's servers when the device is online, as Google documents. Google also documents offline maps for downloaded areas that include driving directions.
What can the provider see? Nothing joinable to you. The origin refuses to boot if any log configuration would serialise coordinates. Rate limiting uses rolling per-minute HMAC tokens instead of your IP. Edge logs keep 24 hours with the IP field masked at ingest. Documented in the published privacy model. Google's documentation describes account-level controls (Timeline, formerly Location History, and Web & App Activity) that govern what location and search activity is saved to the account, and Google has announced that Timeline data is stored on the device.
Offline mode Ed25519-signed region packs from 50 MB (Malta) to 1.5 GB (Germany), verified at download and at every load. Full-offline navigation makes no network connection at all, verifiable by packet trace. In build Google documents downloadable offline areas for the Maps app, which it states must be updated periodically to stay available.
Live traffic None at R·01. R·04 plans an opt-in probe layer that sends OSM segment IDs, speed and hour-of-week with no coordinates, no session and no fine timestamps, published back only when 50 or more contributors are pooled per segment-hour. Off by default, forever. Planned · R·04 Google documents live traffic in the Maps app and describes it as derived from aggregated, anonymised location data from devices that have location services turned on.
Business model Infrastructure inside the products you buy. NAV·IT is included in FuelIT and MapIT at every tier and is never sold, licensed or embedded as a standalone data business, ad platform or third-party SDK. If that ever changes, a superseding ADR appears in git the same day. The consumer app is free to use. Alphabet reports advertising as its largest source of revenue, and Google licenses the Google Maps Platform APIs to developers on usage-based terms it publishes.
Open source Open primitives throughout: OpenStreetMap data, Valhalla routing, Photon geocoding and MapLibre rendering, all under Apache-2, BSD or MIT licences. VF publishes the engineering spec, threat model, privacy model and verification checklist. The origin Ed25519-signs every routing response and clients refuse a tampered one; VF deploys the same signing infrastructure for clients. Proprietary. Google publishes developer SDKs and APIs for the Maps Platform; the app and the map data are Google's own.
Platforms iPhone (iOS 16+), Android 10+ with no Google Play Services dependency (GrapheneOS, /e/OS, LineageOS), PinePhone, and any modern web browser. CarPlay and Android Auto on VF's own map at R·02. The DNS filter from Guardian Shield runs on every VF machine alongside it. CarPlay: R·02 Android, iOS, web, Android Auto and CarPlay, as Google documents.
Jurisdiction Malta, EU. VF Empire Corp Ltd (C 94160), with the origin server in Germany. Sub-processors are listed in the published privacy model; the Terms § 16 warranty applies as on every VF product. Google LLC, United States. Google's terms state that users in the European Economic Area contract with Google Ireland Limited.
Status today In build. R·01 ships inside FuelIT for Germany, France, Spain, Italy, Austria, the United Kingdom, Portugal, Malta and Luxembourg. MapIT as a standalone navigator on the same engine follows at R·03. In build Generally available worldwide; Google Maps has operated since 2005.

Statements about Google Maps are limited to architectural facts Google itself documents (where data is processed, who holds it, business model, open-source status, jurisdiction). VF makes no claim about Google's security, pricing or performance. If Google's documentation changes, write to info@vfempire.com and VF will correct the row.

THE DECISION

Choose by what the route
is allowed to reveal.

Choose Google Maps if

  • You need worldwide coverage, live traffic, public transport and place search today.
  • You use Android Auto or CarPlay now and want a shipping product on the in-dash screen.
  • You already live inside a Google account and are content with the controls Google documents for saved activity.
  • You want a service with two decades of operation behind it.

Choose NAV·IT if

  • Your destination is confidential by profession: journalism, law, activism, or a fleet that owes its drivers privacy.
  • You drive a de-Googled phone or a Linux phone and want a navigator with no dependency on Google Play Services.
  • You want offline to mean offline, with a packet trace to prove it and a bug bounty behind the claim.
  • You use FuelIT or plan to use MapIT, where NAV·IT is included in the price.
  • You want EU jurisdiction, open primitives and Ed25519-signed routing responses you can verify.
  • You accept an in-build product and want to follow the spec, threat model and verification checklist as it ships.

NAV·IT is one of 23 systems on the VF build slate. The two other comparisons follow the same rules: VF Mail vs Proton Mail and Guardian Shield vs Bitwarden. The method behind every VF system is on the software page.

QUESTIONS

Asked.
Answered.

Can I download NAV·IT today?

No. NAV·IT is in build. R·01 ships inside FuelIT for Germany, France, Spain, Italy, Austria, the United Kingdom, Portugal, Malta and Luxembourg, and MapIT follows as a standalone navigator on the same engine at R·03. What is published today is the engineering spec, the threat model, the privacy model and the verification checklist. Register interest on the NAV·IT page and VF writes when the engine opens.

Does NAV·IT work offline?

Yes, and offline means offline. Full-offline mode routes on the device from Ed25519-signed region packs (50 MB for Malta, up to 1.5 GB for Germany) and produces zero network traffic during navigation, which anyone can verify with a packet trace using the published checklist. Hybrid mode, the default, needs no local storage and reaches only navigator.vfempire.com through the anonymising gateway.

Does NAV·IT have live traffic like Google Maps?

No, at R·01. Live traffic on the mainstream services depends on broadcasting device positions, and NAV·IT will not do that. R·04 plans an opt-in probe layer that sends OSM segment IDs, speed and hour-of-week with no coordinates, and publishes the result only when 50 or more contributors are pooled per segment-hour. It stays off by default, forever. Google documents its own traffic layer as derived from aggregated, anonymised location data.

Does NAV·IT run without Google Play Services?

Yes. NAV·IT has no dependency on Google Play Services and runs on GrapheneOS, /e/OS and LineageOS, on the PinePhone, on iOS 16 and later, and in any modern web browser. Android uses the JDK's native Ed25519 to verify each routing response; iOS uses CryptoKit. A tampered or forged response is refused on every platform.

What does NAV·IT cost?

Nothing on its own, because it is never sold on its own. NAV·IT is infrastructure included at every tier of FuelIT and, at R·03, MapIT. VF never monetises it as a standalone data business, an ad platform or an SDK for third parties; if that ever changes, a superseding ADR appears in git the same day. Google Maps is free to consumers, and Google publishes its developer pricing on its own site.

Is NAV·IT a replacement for Google Maps?

For turn-by-turn driving in the nine R·01 countries, on the phones and in the professions listed above, that is the goal. For worldwide coverage, public transport, place reviews and live traffic today, Google Maps offers what NAV·IT does not yet. The honest framing is on the product page: NAV·IT is judged on what a packet capture of a full drive contains, and VF publishes the evidence in git.
